 Judgment

1. In respect of an accident which is not in dispute and the liability of the insurer to pay the compensation is also not in dispute, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums as compensation:

1. 10% future loss of income Rs.1,22,400/-
2. Pain and sufferings Rs.40,000/-

2. The doctor who was examined on behalf of the claimant has stated that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 50% to the left leg and as a consequence, 17% to the whole body.
The Tribunal, however, assessed the disability at 10%.
3. In my view, when the treated doctor has clearly stated that the claimant had suffered 17% disability to the whole body, the Tribunal ought not to have reduced it to 10%.
Consequently, the disability is fixed at 17%.
4. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2014,
would be Rs.8,500/-.
5. As the claimant was aged 28 years, a multiplier of '17' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,73,400/- (Rs.8,500/-
x 12 x 17 x 10%) towards 'loss of future income'.
6.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.15,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities'.

In my view, having regard to the fact that the claimant had suffered 50%
disability to left leg and 17% disability to the whole body, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' and Rs.75,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,81,100/- towards 'medical expenses and other incidental expenses'.
Since, it is based on the documentary evidence, the same is affirmed.
8. The evidence on record indicates that the claimant was hospitalized for 13 days.
In that view of the matter, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'attendant, food and nutrition and conveyance charges'.
9. The Tribunal has treated the laid up period as one month.

Since the claimant has suffered 50%
disability to left leg, it would be appropriate to treat the laid up period as four months and award a sum of Rs.34,000/- (Rs.8,500/- x 4) towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
10. The doctor who treated the claimant has stated that the claimant would need a further surgery which would cost approximately Rs.50,000/-.

However, since no evidence is produced to indicate that the claimant has actually incurred any further expenses, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'future medical expenses'.

11. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

12 . Thus, the claimant is held entitled to a total compensation of Rs.5,83,500/- as against Rs.3,70,500/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
